children: Shares of Miami-based Summit Therapeutics surged about 17% in after-hours trading Monday after AstraZeneca announced it would invest $2 billion in the cancer-drug developer. AstraZeneca's stake would equal around 12% of the company.

The deal centers on ivonescimab, Summit's experimental cancer drug that was initially developed in China. The drug blocks two proteins that help tumors grow and evade the immune system, called PD-1 and VEGF. The FDA is reviewing it for certain lung cancer patients and is due to decide by mid-November. It's not a sure bet: While promising ivonescimab data headlined a major cancer research meeting earlier this year, the drug has drawn some criticism because its studies were largely done in Asia and didn't include the typical age distribution for the disease.
The companies will test ivonescimab with AstraZeneca's antibody-drug conjugate in gastrointestinal cancers.
